Issued at 346 PM CDT Fri Aug 21 2026

Currently through the rest of this afternoon...

Scattered showers and thunderstorms continue to make their way 
southeast across the forecast area today...a trend that will 
continue though mid-late afternoon hours. Looking aloft, upper 
air and satellite data showing this activity being driven by a 
weaker shortwave disturbance sliding out of central SD and into 
NNErn NE. This disturbance is embedded in larger scale 
northwesterly flow set up across the Central/Nrn 
Plains...between ridging extending northward out of the Desert 
SW and broad troughing across the Great Lakes/Midwest region, 
while a larger area of low pressure spins off the Pac NW coast. 
The surface pattern across the forecast area has been a bit of a
messy one throughout the day...between just an overall weaker 
pressure gradient along with any even weak outflow boundaries 
produced by this activity today...winds are variable in 
direction. Most speeds have been around 5-10 MPH, a few spots 
closer to any storms have had gusts closer to 25-30 MPH at least
for a brief time. 

For the rest of this afternoon-early evening...main story will 
continue to lie with continued potential for scattered 
showers/storms pushing SE through and eventually out of the
forecast area. Near/out ahead of this activity, SPC meso page 
showing MLCAPE values exceeding 2000 j/kg, with deeper 
layer/effective shear of at least 30kts. Storms working their 
way SE will continue to have the potential to be 
strong/severe...one thing working against activity is that the 
upper level disturbance/lift just isn't overly strong, which 
isn't helping overcome some lingering capping. Large 
hail/damaging winds would be the primary threats. One good thing
about the scattered nature of this activity is that so far, 
areas that had been on the wetter side over the past few days 
are getting a chance to dry up a bit.

Later tonight on into this weekend...

Once this ongoing activity slides off to our SE, models continue
to show a relative lull across the area through the evening 
hours. Winds should be turning more east-northeasterly, with 
models showing an area of sfc low pressure setting up off to our
west- southwest...but speeds look to remain on the lighter side
overall. A few models try to bring another round of isolated 
activity back into the area already by around 06Z, but there is 
more model support for the timing of the next round of 
showers/storms to be closer to/after 08Z or so. Models showing 
this activity developing into a NW-SE orientated swath across 
the forecast area...tied to another weaker, mainly mid-level 
shortwave disturbance moving through, aided some by 
frontogenetical forcing closer to 850mb. Hi-res models showing 
this elevated activity could have CAPE values around 1500 j/kg 
to tap into, with deeper layer shear around 30-40kts 
possible...keeping the potential for strong-severe storms in 
place. Entire CWA remains in the SPC Day 1 Slight Risk area 
through tonight...large hail and damaging winds remain the 
primary threats, though additional heavy rainfall rates are not 
out of the question as well. 

Not out of the question that some activity could linger into the 
morning hours on Saturday...and uncertainty in the exact timing 
of that departure is not high...but outside of that models are 
in pretty good agreement showing the daytime hours being dry. 
Aloft, models showing continued northwesterly flow across the 
area...if anything that low pressure system currently off the 
Pac NW starts pushing inland, giving the main ridge axis a bit 
of an eastward push. Winds look to remain on the lighter side 
around 10-15 MPH, remaining easterly. Forecast highs are in the 
mid-upper 80s.

Models showing another upper level shortwave disturbance riding 
around the edge of the ridge axis Saturday evening through 
Sunday AM...bringing another chance for showers/storms to the 
entire forecast area. The area is currently not outlooked in the
SPC Day 2 outlook (just in general thunder)...with models 
currently showing the better axis of instability setting up just
off to our west, and deeper layer shear is on the weaker side.

Confidence in precipitation chances Sunday-Sunday night is on
the lower side (outside of any lingering activity from Sat 
night)...with NBM PoPs mainly clipping northern and eastern 
portions of of the forecast area. Models not showing any notable
change in the upper level pattern...and winds turn more 
southerly as sfc troughing develops over the High Plains. 
Forecast highs are more in the upper 70s for central/eastern 
areas, low-mid 80s further west...but that will be dependent on 
timing of any lingering precipitation.

Next week...

Periodic thunderstorm chances remain in the forecast as we get
into the new work week...but honestly, not a ton of confidence
at this point in the timing/tracking of any of the upper level 
disturbances driving these chances. Models show varying
